### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface MetaLayeredRequest))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface MetaLayeredRequest))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface MetaLayeredRequest))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface MetaLayeredRequest))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface MetaLayeredRequest))_
- `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface MetaLayeredRequest))_
- `content/docs/ui/setup-app.mdx`  _(via packageId (symbol, a field of interface MetaLayeredRequest))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via RestServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `69376fb00c7e874cbafe2df2d02302c76f6d9d03` — the merge of head `9d275b85e3c5f624998f6047adc7c5b196c63730` into base `53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 69376fb00c7e874cbafe2df2d02302c76f6d9d03 && git checkout 69376fb00c7e874cbafe2df2d02302c76f6d9d03
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69 9d275b85e3c5f624998f6047adc7c5b196c63730 && git checkout -B drift-repro 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69 && git merge --no-ff 9d275b85e3c5f624998f6047adc7c5b196c63730

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ed6b7108ec0aafd43138f1980d3865cf538e7fe6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-disable-enforcement.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts, packages/rest/src/objectql-slot-consumer-census.test.ts + packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts (the `/layers` route, the item read's `?layers=` branch and its catch), packages/rest/src/index.ts (the exported `MetaItemReadGateSources` and `MetaLayeredRequest`), packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts (the census population), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`domainDeps.getObjectQL`, `getObjectQLService`, `errorFromThrown`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`getMetaItem`, `readMetaItem`, `isItemOfDisabledPackage`, `canonicalizeMetaRequestType`, `servedLockState`, `getMetaItemLayered`, `findServedOverlayRow`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`isPackageDisabled`), packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts (`extractProtection`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-catalog-echo.ts and packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/packaged-permission-set-lock-gate.ts (the direct `getMetaItemLayered` readers), packages/spec/src/api/plugin-rest-api.zod.ts (the declared `/layers` route), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs and .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (the Check Changeset job), content/docs/ui/apps.mdx and content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx (the two hand-written pages naming `/layers`); the two changesets, .changeset/24210-rest-layered-doors-disabled-package.md and .changeset/24210-runtime-layered-doors-disabled-package.md, read as prose for ② only.

Inputs: card #24210 (body; every comment, 6239527781 through 6246528708, including triage 6239967422, the seat ruling 6241893667, the claim 6245752510, the two landings 6243759173 and 6245732037, and this part's `os-dev-report` 6246528708), PR #24223's record 6243449822 and ACCEPT 6243458372, PR #24247's record 6245404399 and ACCEPT 6245503059, the #7557 pin's docblock, PR #24267's body, file list and its one comment (the Docs Drift Check 6246519425; no review comments and no reviews), the net diff `origin/main` a422f04fe0 (fetched fresh; merge-base fb6fb24e2f, the main this head merged) to the head (9 files, +449/-21), and the 39 check-runs on the head.

Check-runs at read time (2026-10-18T06:32:44Z): 39 runs; 27 `success`, 6 `skipped`, 6 `in_progress`, 0 `failure`. `success`: Build Core (06:25:47Z), TypeScript Type Check and Type Check workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint and Repo Gates and its seven Lint legs, Check Changeset (06:23:15Z), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregate), the four PR-claim checks ("The card this PR closes must claim this branch" and "Part-of PR must not also close its card" among them), Auto Label, filter. `in_progress`, recorded as seen and not waited for: Test Core (1/6) through (6/6). `skipped` by path or opt-in filter: Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood shards placeholder and Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke. The build, type-check, lint and changeset families are answered green; the test family is the seat's to read before the queue (③.11).

### ① Derived judgments

**A. One step, one chain, four doors.** `createMetaLayeredAnswer` has exactly two callers at this head, `RestServer.serveMetaItemLayered` (rest-server.ts 4190) and the dispatcher's `answerMetaLayered` (meta.ts 883), and those two serve all four doors: REST `GET /meta/:type/:name/layers` (meta-item-read-routes.ts 307, after `refuseUnknownQueryParams`, the masker and the `getMetaItemLayered` probe) and the item read's `?layers=` branch (551, after `wantsMetaItemLayers` and the deprecation headers); the dispatcher's three-segment `layers` branch (meta.ts 1189) and its item read's `wantsMetaItemLayers` branch (1782). The declared route in `plugin-rest-api.zod.ts` (`handler: 'getMetaItemLayered'`) is a description; nothing in rest, runtime or core dispatches a protocol method by that name, so no third owner serves the path. Step 1b sits after step 1 (`present.length === 0` is `absent`) and before step 2 (`createMetaItemReadGate`), so an author whose `mayWriteItem` is true never reaches the gate for a withheld item: pinned on REST with the real `metaSaveVerdict` (the author served the nav whole and the member pruned while enabled, both answered the missing name after the disable, each restored to its own view after the re-enable). The guard `metaType !== 'object' && metaType !== 'package'` is evaluated before the source is called, so objects and packages pay no engine resolution and no plain read. Right.

**B. The source is optional, and an absent source withholds nothing.** The step reads `await sources.isItemOfDisabledPackage?.(…) === true`: an interface without the member answers `undefined`, which is not `true`, so a host that builds its own `MetaItemReadGateSources` (exported from `@objectstack/rest`, index.ts 175) answers as before, with no crash. Both in-repo implementers wire it: `RestServer.metaItemReadGateSources` (rest-server.ts 3521-3544) and the dispatcher's `metaItemReadGateSources` (meta.ts 513-537). `MetaListAnswerSources` and `MetaItemAnswerSources` extend the same interface and receive the member from the same builders, but the chain's step (meta-item-read-gate.ts 3810) is the only read site, so the list and item chains are unchanged. Right.

**C. The owner read is the by-name read's own field and predicate.** On REST: `p.getMetaItem({ type, name, packageId?, environmentId? })`, then `registry.isPackageDisabled(envelope?.packageId) === true`; on the dispatcher: `protocol.getMetaItem({ type, name, packageId? })`, then `isServiceItemOfDisabledPackage(registry, { _packageId: owner })`, which is `registry.isPackageDisabled(owner) === true` (meta.ts 254). Field identity at this head: `getMetaItem` (protocol.ts 11099-11110) asks `isItemOfDisabledPackage(this.engine?.registry, answer.item)`, i.e. `registry.isPackageDisabled(answer.item._packageId)`; the envelope's `packageId` is `servedLockState(…, decorated, …).packageId` (11619-11641), `servedLockState` (17946) reads `extractProtection(document).packageId`, which is `document._packageId` (metadata-protection.zod.ts 174), and `document` is `decorated`, the same `answer.item`. The withheld answer keeps that envelope and drops only `item` and `registration` (11109-11110). `readMetaItem` grafts the stored row's `package_id` onto the item when it carries none (11263 on the draft arm, 11324-11325 on the active arm), which is why a runtime-saved item, whose layered answer names no owner (H1), still names it on the plain read. `registry.isPackageDisabled(undefined)` is `false` (registry.ts 5394-5398), so an unowned item is served. The predicate is the one `getMetaItems`, `getMetaItem` and `listDrafts` ask (protocol.ts 10411, 11105, 25570). One field, one predicate, four doors: right, and option A of the report's first open question is the right one; B would leave the runtime-saved shape, the only shape a live server can disable, served.

**D. The `?package=` scope.** `MetaLayeredRequest.packageId` is the scope each transport already parsed (`metaItemPackageBinding(req.query?.package)`, `all` naming no package) and handed to `getMetaItemLayered`; the chain hands it to the source, which hands it to `getMetaItem`. Both protocol reads resolve the overlay row through one function, `findServedOverlayRow` (protocol.ts 11293 and 11307 in `readMetaItem`, 11870 in `getMetaItemLayered`), at the same address (`request.packageId` or `packagelessReadAddress`), so the owner asked about is the owner of the copy the layered read served, scoped or not. Pinned on REST with the real protocol (`twin_dash` stored in both packages: the healthy copy served under its own scope on both spellings, the disabled copy absent under its own) and on the dispatcher (the scope reaches `getMetaItem`, asserted with `toHaveBeenCalledWith`; the unscoped read resolves the disabled copy and is absent). Right; the one-property edits in `serveMetaItemLayered` and `answerMetaLayered` are what carries it (③.1).

**E. What the extra read costs and can throw.** It is paid only after step 1 (a missing name pays nothing), only for non-object, non-package types, and only once an engine with `isPackageDisabled` is in hand (an unwired host or a predicate-less registry returns `false` before the plain read). The read is `getMetaItem` whole: one store resolution plus the lock state, and for `app` keyed by a package id an extra list read. It can throw a store outage or a spelling refusal from `canonicalizeMetaRequestType` (400 `INVALID_REQUEST`); `objectPackageDisabledError` and `noPendingDraftError` are unreachable here (no object, no draft state), and a spelling the plain read refuses is one the layered read refused first with the same canonicaliser, so no new spelling fault reaches a caller. Every throw propagates: on REST `serveMetaItemLayered` catches nothing, so the `/layers` route's `handleRouteError` (meta-item-read-routes.ts 346) and the item read's catch (1061-1065: `thrownAnswerIsBareNotFound`, then `handleRouteError`) render it as itself; a rejecting engine slot is `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` from `wiredEngineOrLoud` (rest-server.ts 1560), `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, pinned on both spellings with the item's label absent from the body. On the dispatcher the chain runs inside `answerMetaLayered`'s `try`, whose `catch` is the door's existing `errorFromThrown(e, 500)`: a 503-shaped throw is 503 (pinned), a 400-shaped one 400, a shapeless one 500, exactly what a throw of the layered read already answered there. No throw is read as "not withheld", and none reaches the caller as a layered view. Right. One asymmetry named: the dispatcher's plain item read falls back to 404 for a shapeless throw (`errorFromThrown(e, 404)`, meta.ts 1995) where its layered door falls back to 500; pre-existing on the layered door's catch, not new (③.8).

**F. The resolution readers keep serving.** `getMetaItemLayered` is not in the diff (protocol.ts is untouched). Its direct readers at this head: plugin-security's `echoSecurityCatalogMutation` (security-catalog-echo.ts 194) and `echoStoredSecurityCatalogOverlays` (287), `registerPackagedPermissionSetLockGate` (packaged-permission-set-lock-gate.ts 83), REST's `fetchCurrentMetaDocument` (rest-server.ts 3636), and both transports' `/published` (rest-server.ts 6495, meta.ts 1306). None goes through the chain. Pinned two ways: the READERS table gains three `enforces: false` rows (the producer for `app`, the producer for `permission`, the plain read's kept `packageId`), and the REST pin asserts `protocol.getMetaItemLayered(...).effective` still resolves for every withheld specimen on the real protocol and real `SchemaRegistry`. Right; ruling 6241893667 Q1 A holds.

**G. The object row and `package`.** Unchanged: `getMetaItemLayered` throws `objectPackageDisabledError` before any layer (protocol.ts 11751-11753), rendered by the route catch as `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` on both transports, pinned equal to the plain read on REST and through `expectObjectRefusal` on the dispatcher; the step's type guard never asks the source for an object. `package` is excluded by the same guard. Right.

**H. The census.** `objectQLProvider` invocation sites at this head: rest-server.ts 3097 (`computeExecCtx`), 3530 (this step), 6249 (`/state`), 6483 (`/published`), batch-routes.ts 171: five, all through `wiredEngineOrLoud`. The census counts five and §3 cites the pin file for `/published`, `/layers` and `?layers=true`. Right.

**I. Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged.** (1) REST `/layers` and `?layers=true` for a disabled package's non-object, non-package item: the served set narrows to the missing name's answer, for every caller: right. (2) The dispatcher's two spellings, the same: right. (3) REST gains a `503` arm on those two doors when a wired engine slot rejects (the decidable test every slot consumer passes): right. (4) Both transports answer a plain-read fault on those doors as itself (E): right. (5) `MetaItemReadGateSources.isItemOfDisabledPackage` and `MetaLayeredRequest.packageId`, both optional, both exported from `@objectstack/rest`: additive to implementers and callers, named in the rest changeset: right. (6) No spec change, no error code, no new protocol method, no route body; `getMetaItemLayered` and `fetchCurrentMetaDocument` untouched: right. (7) The merge commit brings main's `fb6fb24e2f` (slice 13c and a runtime body-parsing change); main has since moved three commits, none touching `packages/rest/src`, `packages/runtime/src`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src` or `packages/objectql/src`, so no symbol this diff reads has moved under it.

**What each door answers now** (a disabled package's non-object item | triage's answer | a missing name), on this head, author and member alike:
- REST `GET /meta/TYPE/NAME/layers`: `404`, `sendMetaItemAbsent`'s nested `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` body; status, body and headers pinned `toEqual` the missing name's | absence | the same bytes.
- REST `GET /meta/TYPE/NAME?layers=true`: the same, with `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` naming the item's own path, the one difference from the missing name's answer, whose `Link` names its own path | absence | the same bytes.
- Dispatcher `GET /meta/TYPE/NAME/layers`: `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND "Not found"`, the item read's own absence, pinned byte-equal (status, headers, body) to the missing name's | absence | the same bytes.
- Dispatcher `GET /meta/TYPE/NAME?layers=true`: the same, with `Deprecation` and `Link` | absence | the same bytes.
- Author against member: enabled, the author reads the stored app whole and the member pruned (ruling 5856774816, unchanged); disabled, both read the missing name's answer on both spellings; re-enabled, each reads what it read before (pinned on REST; the chain is one, so the dispatcher follows).
- Objects on both spellings, both transports: `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, unchanged | the object answer | `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`.
- `?package=` naming an enabled package's copy of a shared name: served (200) on both spellings; naming the disabled package's copy: the missing name's answer.
- Unwired engine, or a registry without the predicate: served as before #24210 (pinned on both transports). A wired engine that rejects: REST `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (pinned); the dispatcher served as before (③.4).
- The producer `getMetaItemLayered`, the echo and the lock gate: served (pinned).

### ② Semver level

- Two changesets, `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/runtime`, each `minor`, each **BREAKING** with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and the adr-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. `minor` is the launch-window level `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces for a breaking change ("During the launch window we ship breaking changes as `minor`", its header), and the marker's reasoning holds: no stored shape, key, export or code moves, and re-enabling restores the reads (pinned on both transports). Each body matches the diff: the rest changeset's "to every caller, an author who may write the item included" is ①.A; its owner sentence is ①.C and ①.D; its "Added, optional" names exactly the two optional members, and "a host that supplies neither answers as before" is ①.B; its "Unchanged" names the producer and its two plugin readers (①.F). The runtime changeset's "as `RestServer` asks it" is ①.C, and "Objects already answered `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` here" has been true since PR #24208 and PR #24223. The title carries `!`.
- No `@objectstack/objectql` changeset: its diff is a test file outside the published `files`. Right.
- The PR body's `Clause-②: no (narrowing) (owes one ... review before the queue)` is the claim's spelling verbatim at a line start, the spelling `readClause2Line` read as `no` and `narrowing` on PR #24247; no new key lands on any published payload (the two added members are TypeScript interface members of `@objectstack/rest`, not wire keys). The face is narrowing, hence this tier.
- CI's verdict: `Check Changeset` `success` on this head (06:23:15Z); that job runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base MERGE_BASE` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base MERGE_BASE` (pr-automation.yml 977 and 1127).
- One prose gap, no level change: neither changeset spells that the two doors now also answer a plain-read fault as itself, or REST's `503` arm on a rejecting engine slot (①.E, ①.I 3-4); the PR body names both (H2 and the Acceptance notes). The same gap was accepted on PR #24247 without a changeset edit; a one-sentence addendum is the most that is owed (③.6).

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Fence deviation, the one-property `packageId` edits in `serveMetaItemLayered` and `answerMetaLayered`** (report deviation 1): accepted as right. `serveMetaItemLayered` is a `RestServer` class member (rest-server.ts 4152), outside `registerMetadataEndpointsInner`; no route body is edited, and neither `meta-item-read-routes.ts` nor `meta-collection-routes.ts` is in the file list. `answerMetaLayered` is in the file the claim names. The edit is what the measured two-package collision requires (①.D): option B (an unscoped owner read, as `/published` reads) withholds an enabled package's copy under its own `?package=`; option C re-parses, in two transports, a query the caller already parsed. Open PR #24257 (slice 13c) edits `registerMetadataEndpointsInner`'s write routes, disjoint from this member; the merge at this head is textually clean and main has not touched these files since.
2. **Fence deviation, `objectql-slot-consumer-census.test.ts`** (report deviation 2): accepted as right. The census exists to make each new `objectQLProvider` consumer examined on arrival; it went red at 4 before the edit and counts five with §3 naming the pin (①.H). The same move was accepted on the second half (record 6245404399 ③.6).
3. **H1 falsified for a runtime-saved item, the owner source** (open question 1): answered, A is right (①.C). The layered envelope's `packageId` and the layers' `_packageId` come from the code layer's artifact, so an overlay-only item names no owner there, while the plain read grafts the stored row's `package_id` (`readMetaItem` 11324-11325) and keeps the envelope when it withholds. Reading the owner off the layered answer (B) would serve exactly the shape a live server can disable (a code package refuses the disable over HTTP: `422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`, measured). Nothing owed.
4. **The dispatcher's `getObjectQLService` fail-open on an unresolvable engine** (open question 3 and the report's out-of-scope finding): answered for this card, escalated as a seat question. Read at this head: `domainDeps.getObjectQL` (http-dispatcher.ts 550) is `getObjectQLService` (2781), whose `catch` answers `null` for a failed `resolveService('objectql')`, and the source reads `null` as "no registry to ask" and withholds nothing. REST's `wiredEngineOrLoud` answers the same condition `503`, and its own docblock records the KERNEL branch of that seam as RESIDUE: `kernel.getServiceAsync('objectql')` rejects with a bare `Error` both when the service was never registered and when it was registered and failed to construct, which is why REST does not make that branch loud either. So on the dispatcher a failed engine resolution serves a disabled package's layered view as before #24210, as its `/published` owner check (PR #24247, meta.ts 1287) already does. It is an existing property of a seam every dispatcher domain reads through, not a wrong answer this diff introduces, and the composition it affects (a kernel whose `objectql` service is registered and fails to construct) is an outage with wider symptoms than this door. Not a blocker. For the seat: option B, a card to make the dispatcher's engine seam tell "not wired" from "failed", is the `@objectstack/core` registry change REST's residue note already names; the report's dedupe words are the right ones.
5. **The `?package=` scope** (open question 2): answered, A is right (①.D). The scope rides into the owner read as a fact of the chain's request, so the two transports cannot drift; pinned on both.
6. **Changeset prose** (②): the plain-read fault and REST's `503` arm are named in the PR body and not in the changesets; the seat may fold one sentence into each at queue time or accept the body's naming, as on PR #24247. Not a blocker.
